theory.intro: A **scale drawing** — a map, plan or blueprint — is a similar figure of a real object. The scale is written as a ratio **image : original**, usually in the form $1:n$, meaning every $1$ unit on the drawing represents $n$ units in real life. To move between the drawing and real life you multiply or divide by $n$, after making both lengths the same unit.
facts: A scale of $1:n$ means $1$ unit on the drawing represents $n$ units in real life.
$\text{real length}=\text{drawing length}\times n$, and $\text{drawing length}=\text{real length}\div n$.
Convert both lengths to the same unit before comparing, then give the answer in a sensible unit.
To find the scale from a matched pair, write $\text{drawing}:\text{real}$ in the same unit and simplify to $1:n$.
A scale written the larger way round, $n:1$, is a magnification — the drawing is larger than the real object, used for tiny things like cells.
steps: Write the scale as a ratio, image : original.
Decide whether the known length is on the drawing (image) or in real life (original).
Multiply or divide by the scale number, then convert to an appropriate unit.

foundation.question_text: A scale drawing is made so that $1$ cm on the drawing represents $2$ m in real life. Write this scale as a ratio in simplest form.
On a plan, $5$ mm represents $20$ m in real life. Write this scale as a ratio in simplest form.
A map has a scale of $1:500$. A road is $24$ mm long on the map. Find the real length of the road, in metres.
A plan has a scale of $1:200$. A path measures $7$ cm on the plan. Find the real length of the path, in metres.
A map has a scale of $1:5000$. Two landmarks are $250$ m apart in real life. Find the distance between them on the map, in centimetres.
You draw a scale diagram of a tree using a scale of $1:150$. The tree is $45$ m high. How high should the tree be in your drawing, in centimetres?
A length of $4$ cm on a scale drawing represents $20$ m in real life. Find the scale of the drawing, in the form $1:n$.
A scientist draws a cell using a scale of $100:1$. The drawing of the cell is $8$ cm long. Find the real length of the cell, in millimetres.

development.question_text: A map has a scale of $1:50\,000$. Two towns are $17$ cm apart on the map. Find the real distance between them, in kilometres.
A map has a scale of $1:25\,000$. A walking trail is $3.4$ cm long on the map. Find the real length of the trail, in metres.
A map has a scale of $1:100\,000$. Two towns are $66$ km apart in real life. Find the distance between them on the map, in centimetres.
A length of $32$ cm on a blueprint represents $1600$ m in real life. Find the scale of the blueprint, in the form $1:n$.
A real-life distance of $1.5$ km is represented by $60$ cm on a plan. Find the scale of the plan, in the form $1:n$.
A scientist draws a bacterium using a scale of $500:1$. The real bacterium is $0.01$ mm long. How long should the bacterium be in the drawing, in millimetres?

mastery.solution_text:
$4\text{ cm}:8\text{ m}$
$=4\text{ cm}:800\text{ cm}$
$=1:200$
$\text{real}=6\times200$
$=1200\text{ cm}$
$=12\text{ m}$

mastery.question_text: A rectangular room on a house plan of scale $1:100$ measures $5$ cm by $4$ cm. Find the real area of the room, in square metres.
A student magnifies a drawing of an ant so that the drawing is larger than the real ant, and writes the scale as $1:50$. Explain what is wrong, and give the scale written correctly.
mastery.solution_text: A magnified drawing is larger than the real object, so the image length is greater than the original length. Written as image : original the larger number must come first, so the scale should be $50:1$, not $1:50$.
